newsitem.title: bangladesh: Cyclone batters Bangladesh coast, 500,000 evacuated.
newsitem.headline: Cyclone batters Bangladesh coast, 500,000 evacuated.

text.p: A severe cyclone from the Bay of Bengal lashed the Bangladesh coast on Monday, demolishing homes in its path and forcing the evacuation of more than half a million people.
There was no word on casualties as the cyclone pounded the Cox's Bazar and Teknaf areas, the country's southernmost tip, with winds of more than 200 kph (124 mph), officials said.

But officials feared heavy loss of life and property damage, saying the impact at some places could be greater than the disaster-prone country's worst cyclone in 1991, which killed at least 138,000 people and left millions homeless.

"At some places like Cox's Bazar, the impact of the cyclone could be more fierce than in the 1991 cyclone," said Golam Rabbani of the Cyclone Preparedness Centre in Chittagong, to the north of Cox's Bazar.
The government ordered a disaster alert and evacuation efforts were in full swing as the cyclone hit the country's flat coastal region, officials said.
"The core of the cyclone has yet to arrive, but the wind speed has already passed 200 kph," said Cox's Bazar district administrator Ali Imam Majumder, quoting the local weather office.

"Vast areas have been affected, with electricity supply and telecommunications disrupted. Many houses have been destroyed and we can see sheets of tin from roof tops flying like tree leaves," Majumder told Reuters.
Weather officials said the core of the cyclone could trigger a tidal surge of up to five metres (16 ft).
Authorities fear high seas will inundate large low-lying areas in the South Asian country.
The worst affected areas so far lie in the west of the country, near the border with Burma.

Officials said the main port city of Chittagong was battered by winds of more than 100 (62 mph). Electricity in the city had been disrupted, roads were jammed by fallen trees and electric poles, and the sky was full of flying debris.

More than 33,000 Red Crescent workers and other volunteers were helping the evacuation of people on the coast and offshore islands. More than 160,000 people were moved to shelters in the Cox's Bazar district alone.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina cancelled a planned trip to Spain on Sunday night as the government put the army and navy on high alert for emergency rescue and relief operations.
Air force planes from a Chittagong base were moved to Dhaka while the navy sent vessels to safety.
Telecommunications with Teknaf and Cox's Bazar had been cut.

The Saint Martin's island near Teknaf was under two metres of (six ft) water. Several other islands had been battered by the cyclone and could be inundated, Red Crescent officials said, quoting field volunteers.
Rice crops and shrimp beds were likely to be affected, agriculture officials said.

"There are no significant crops, except for some rice, in the fields now, but shrimp cultivation may be badly affected," said M.A. Wadud, chairman of the Bangladesh Agriculture Development Corporation.
The country earned $265 million through exporting shrimps in 1995-96, Masudur Rahman, a fishery ministry official, said.
Fishermen have been warned not to leave port.
Dozens of ships berthed at Chittagong and Mongla ports were moved to outer anchorages, port officials said.
"We are taking this precaution so the ships do not collide during the storm and jam the channel by sinking," said Chittagong Port Harbourmaster Quamrul Islam.
As state-run radio and television broadcast frequent storm warnings, hundreds of women held open-air prayers in Dhaka seeking divine protection.
People fleeing their homes or being moved to cyclone shelters had been asked to store drinking water, food and other essentials underground to help them after the cyclone.
